question: Which natural formation in northwest India initiates a low pressure area during the summer months?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thar Desert**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Thar Desert**, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is located in the northwestern part of India, primarily in the state of **Rajasthan**, and extends into parts of Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana.
 
• During the **summer months**, the Thar Desert experiences high temperatures, often exceeding 50°C. This intense heat causes the air above the desert to expand and rise, leading to the formation of a **low-pressure area**.
 
• The low-pressure area formed in the Thar Desert plays a significant role in influencing the **Indian monsoon**. It acts as a major driver that attracts moisture-laden winds from the southwest, facilitating the onset of monsoon rains in India.
 
• The rising hot air in the Thar Desert leads to the creation of a **pressure gradient**, which is instrumental in pulling in the moist winds from the Arabian Sea, thereby contributing to monsoon rainfall across the Indian subcontinent.
